supporting: 67-year-old male with persistent occipital headache for 2 days
Headache is the only documented symptom; no specific features of a primary headache syndrome are recorded
opposing: Age 67 and history of hypertension (Riwayat HT) are risk factors for secondary headache
No vital signs, physical examination, or results recorded to confirm primary headache or exclude secondary causes

supporting: Persistent headache for 2 days without documented red flags (not examined)
opposing: Occipital location, age 67, and hypertension may suggest secondary headache
No documented features of tension-type headache (e.g., bilateral, pressing, mild, no vomiting) and no examination to exclude secondary causes
No blood pressure recorded; headache may or may not be related to hypertension

supporting: Persistent occipital headache in a 67-year-old with hypertension
opposing: No thunderclap onset, meningeal signs, or focal deficits recorded; however these were not examined
No focal neurologic deficit or altered consciousness recorded; not examined

supporting: Age 67, hypertension, posterior headache could be posterior circulation ischemia
opposing: No focal deficit, visual symptoms, or neurologic examination recorded
No fever, neck stiffness, or altered mental status recorded; not examined

Headache characteristics: thunderclap onset, severity, associated nausea/vomiting, photophobia/phonophobia, fever, neck stiffness, confusion, seizure, visual loss

nextBestActions.item: Ask about red-flag symptoms: thunderclap onset, focal deficit, fever, neck stiffness, confusion, seizure, visual loss, jaw claudication, and visual symptoms.
nextBestActions.reason: Rule out secondary headache causes in a 67-year-old male with hypertension and persistent occipital headache.

nextBestActions.item: Perform physical examination documenting blood pressure in both arms, heart rate, respiratory rate, SpO2, temperature, Glasgow Coma Scale, NIHSS, focal neurologic deficits, pupillary exam, fundoscopy, meningeal signs, temporal artery tenderness, jaw claudication, visual symptoms, cardiac exam, lung exam, extremity edema, skin rash.
nextBestActions.reason: Initial priority is to obtain vital signs and focused neurologic examination, then rule out secondary headache causes.

nextBestActions.item: Request hematology: hemoglobin, hematocrit, white blood cells, platelet count.
nextBestActions.reason: Laboratory diagnostics as part of secondary headache workup.

nextBestActions.item: Request chemistry/renal/electrolytes: sodium, potassium, chloride, bicarbonate, urea nitrogen, creatinine, glucose, calcium total, magnesium, phosphate.
nextBestActions.reason: Laboratory diagnostics as part of secondary headache workup.

nextBestActions.item: Request liver/protein: ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, total bilirubin, albumin, total protein.
